territorial_scope.description: Federal statute applying to any person engaging in conduct in or affecting United States commerce; enforced by the FTC and FCC.

evidence.quote: engage in a deceptive act or practice in or affecting commerce

summary.short: Proposed federal bill making AI-enabled impersonation fraud, including voice or image replication, unlawful; requires disclosure when AI emulating a human is used in calls or texts; extends telemarketing and robocall rules to text messages; directs FTC and FCC reports and an advisory group.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill would make it unlawful under Sec. 3(a)(1) for any person to engage in deceptive impersonation of a government, business or official, to replicate an individual's image or voice, including with artificial intelligence and with intent to defraud, or to knowingly provide substantial assistance to such conduct. Sec. 3(a)(2) treats violations as violations of an FTC unfair or deceptive practices rule, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission with its FTC Act powers. Sec. 3(b) amends the Seniors Fraud Prevention Act to add information about AI-enabled scams to an advisory office's remit. Sec. 4 extends the Telemarketing Act to text messages and video conference calls, requires disclosure when AI emulating a human is used in calls or texts, and adds a parallel disclosure duty to Communications Act section 227. Sec. 5 authorizes FTC web portal updates and complaint procedures, establishes a joint FTC-FCC AI Scam Prevention Advisory Group that terminates five years after enactment, requires FTC reports within 180 days and FCC regulations within 270 days. The bill states no penalty amounts of its own.

relations.note: Amends section 227 (definition of artificial or prerecorded voice, text message provisions, new subsection (k) on AI disclosure, and subsections (h), (i) and (j) per Sec. 5(d)) and section 230(e), per Sec. 4(b).

relations.target_text: Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.; section 18(a)(1)(B), 15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B))
relations.note: Sec. 3(a)(2) treats a violation of the new impersonation subsection as a violation of a rule under FTC Act section 18(a)(1)(B) and applies the FTC Act's powers, penalties and privileges to its enforcement.

relations.target_text: part 310 of title 16, Code of Federal Regulations
relations.note: Sec. 4(b)(2) provides that the amendments to section 230(e) do not limit the application of the Telemarketing Act or part 310 of title 16 CFR (or successor regulations).

notes: Bill as introduced; the document contains no sponsor, committee or legislative-history record, so no legislative events are coded here. Target instrument IDs are null because the text gives no registry IDs. Sec. 5(a) directs the FTC actions with 'may', while Sec. 5(b) and 5(c) use mandatory wording. Sec. 4(a)(2) and Sec. 4(b)(1)(C) both impose AI disclosure duties in different statutes, the second also reaching text messages. Sec. 5(d)(4) requires FCC rules within 270 days of enactment. Some paragraph numbering in Sec. 5(b) is not indented in the source; the printed numbering is used.
